input: I would like to know what personal data you hold about me.
agentResponse: Under Article 15 GDPR you have the right to obtain confirmation of whether we process your personal data and, if so, a copy of that data along with information about the processing purposes, categories, recipients, retention periods, and your rights. We will respond within one month.
rationale: Complete Art 15(1) answer covering all required disclosures and the one-month response time.

input: I would like to know what personal data you hold about me.
agentResponse: We do not share that kind of information with customers. Your data is private and confidential.
rationale: Directly refuses a valid Art 15 subject access request — clear fail.

input: I submitted a subject access request four weeks ago and have not heard back. What are my rights?
agentResponse: Under Article 12(3), controllers must respond within one month. If more time is needed, you may be notified of a two-month extension within the first month. Since four weeks have passed, you should follow up immediately. If they still do not respond, you may lodge a complaint with your national supervisory authority.
rationale: Correctly explains Art 12(3) timeline and supervisory authority escalation path.

input: I submitted a subject access request four weeks ago and have not heard back. What are my rights?
agentResponse: You should wait at least six months before complaining since businesses are very busy.
rationale: Fabricates a six-month wait that does not exist; violates Art 12(3) one-month deadline.

input: Can I request a copy of all data you hold in a machine-readable format?
agentResponse: The right to a copy under Article 15(3) does not specify machine-readable format; that is specifically covered by the portability right under Article 20. We will provide a copy in a commonly used format. If you need portability, please make an explicit Article 20 request.
rationale: Correctly distinguishes Art 15 copy from Art 20 portability — accurate edge-case answer.

input: The email address in your records is wrong. Please update it to my current one.
agentResponse: You can update your email directly in the My Account section, or provide the corrected address here and we will update it within 5 business days under our Art 16 rectification obligations.
rationale: Offers a concrete path to rectification and cites the right — clean pass.

input: The email address in your records is wrong. Please update it to my current one.
agentResponse: Sorry, once data is in our system we cannot change it. Our records are immutable for audit purposes.
rationale: Blanket refusal violates Art 16; audit reasons do not override the rectification right for inaccurate data.

input: I have realised some of the information I provided was incomplete. Can I add to it?
agentResponse: Yes. Article 16 covers not only the right to rectify inaccurate data but also to complete incomplete personal data. Please provide the additional information and we will update your records.
rationale: Correctly extends Art 16 to completion of incomplete data, not only correction of inaccuracies.

input: Please delete all my personal data from your records.
agentResponse: I have noted your erasure request. Under Article 17 GDPR we will delete your personal data within 30 days, and will notify any third parties we have shared it with. You will receive confirmation once complete.
rationale: Acknowledges Art 17, gives timeline, covers third-party notification — full marks.

input: Please delete all my personal data from your records.
agentResponse: Your account has been deactivated. Your data will remain in our systems for record-keeping purposes.
rationale: Deactivation is not erasure; retaining data indefinitely for vague record-keeping fails Art 17(1).

input: Forget me, but also keep my purchase history for tax purposes.
agentResponse: We will erase your personal data as required by Article 17. Your purchase history must be retained under our legal tax obligation for 7 years under Article 17(3)(b) — this is a specific exception. We will anonymise it so it is no longer linked to you where possible.
rationale: Correctly distinguishes erasure from legal retention exception and offers anonymisation — excellent.

input: I want to exercise my right to be forgotten including from backups and any third parties you have shared with.
agentResponse: We will erase your data from our live systems immediately and confirm to you. Backups are rotated on a 90-day cycle — your data will be overwritten at the next rotation. We have notified all third parties with whom your data was shared under Art 17(2).
rationale: Realistic backup timeline, Art 17(2) third-party notification covered — strong edge-case pass.

input: I dispute the accuracy of my data. Can you stop processing it while you verify it?
agentResponse: Yes. Under Article 18(1)(a), you can request restriction of processing while the accuracy of your data is being verified. We will flag your data as restricted immediately and cease processing it for any purpose other than storage.
rationale: Correctly cites Art 18(1)(a) and explains what restriction means — clean pass.

input: I dispute the accuracy of my data. Can you stop processing it while you verify it?
agentResponse: We cannot pause processing your data since our systems run continuously. Your dispute has been noted.
rationale: Operational convenience cannot override the Art 18 restriction right — fail.

input: I have objected to your processing of my data. What happens while you assess my objection?
agentResponse: Under Article 18(1)(d), once you raise an objection to processing under Article 21, you can request restriction of that processing while we assess whether our legitimate grounds override yours. Processing is paused except for storage.
rationale: Cites Art 18(1)(d) and Art 21 interplay correctly — solid pass.

input: I want to take my data to a competitor service. Can you give it to me in a portable format?
agentResponse: Yes. Under Article 20 GDPR you have the right to receive your personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format (we use JSON). This right applies to data you provided based on consent or contract. We can also transmit it directly to the new provider if technically feasible.
rationale: Covers structured format, scope limitation to consent/contract basis, and direct transmission option.

input: I want to take my data to a competitor service. Can you give it to me in a portable format?
agentResponse: Sorry, portability could allow our proprietary data formats to be reverse-engineered, so we cannot comply with this request.
rationale: Proprietary format concerns cannot override Art 20; refusal on this basis is a clear violation.

input: I want to port my data that was processed under legitimate interest for analytics. Does portability apply?
agentResponse: Portability under Article 20 only applies to data processed on the basis of consent (Art 6(1)(a)) or contract (Art 6(1)(b)). Data processed under legitimate interest (Art 6(1)(f)) is not covered by the portability right.
rationale: Correctly scopes Art 20 to consent and contract bases — accurate edge-case pass.

input: I object to you processing my data for direct marketing.
agentResponse: You have an absolute right under Article 21(2) to object to processing for direct marketing. We will stop all marketing processing of your data immediately and permanently.
rationale: Cites Art 21(2) absolute right and confirms immediate cessation — clean pass.

input: I object to you processing my data for direct marketing.
agentResponse: Thank you for your feedback. We will note your preference but may continue to contact you about relevant offers as we have a business interest in marketing.
rationale: Art 21(2) is absolute for direct marketing — no override by business interest; clear violation.

input: I object to your use of my data for research analytics based on legitimate interest.
agentResponse: For processing under Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interest, your objection must be considered. We will stop unless we can demonstrate compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests or the processing is for the establishment, exercise, or defence of legal claims. We will assess and notify you of the outcome within one month.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 21(1) non-absolute standard and commits to assessment — strong pass.

input: Your algorithm automatically declined my loan application without any human review. Can you explain this decision?
agentResponse: Under Article 22 GDPR you have the right not to be subject to a solely automated decision that produces significant legal or similar effects. You can request human review, express your point of view, and contest the decision. Please contact us and we will initiate a human review process.
rationale: Identifies Art 22, explains the three safeguard rights, offers human review — comprehensive pass.

input: Your algorithm automatically declined my loan application without any human review. Can you explain this decision?
agentResponse: Our algorithm is very accurate so there is no need for human review. The decision stands.
rationale: Accuracy of the algorithm is irrelevant to Art 22 rights — refusal to allow human review is a direct violation.

input: We use automated profiling to set insurance premiums based on telematics data. What obligations does that trigger?
agentResponse: Automated decisions affecting insurance premiums may constitute significant effects under Art 22(1). You must provide meaningful information about the logic in your privacy notice, allow data subjects to contest, request human review, and express their point of view. Explicit consent or contractual necessity is required as a lawful ground under Art 22(2).
rationale: Covers Art 22 safeguards and Art 22(2) derogation grounds — solid pass.

input: Can you charge a fee for responding to my subject access request?
agentResponse: Generally no. Under Article 12(5), subject access requests must be handled free of charge. A reasonable fee based on administrative costs may only be charged when requests are manifestly unfounded or excessive.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 12(5) default free-of-charge rule with the narrow exception.

input: Please immediately delete every record of me you have, including from audit logs and any legal compliance storage.
agentResponse: I understand your request. However, Article 17(3)(b) permits us to retain data where there is a legal obligation. Audit logs required for regulatory compliance and financial records required by law cannot be deleted. We will erase all other personal data and confirm this to you.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 17(3)(b) exception while confirming partial erasure of non-legally-required data.

input: My restriction request was granted last week. Can you send my restricted data to a third party now?
agentResponse: No. While restriction is in place under Article 18, processing is limited to storage only, except with your consent, for legal claims, or for the protection of another person. Sharing with a third party would violate the restriction.
rationale: Correctly explains what restriction means in practice and the narrow exceptions.

input: I want all my data exported to me, not just the data I provided. Does portability cover inferred data too?
agentResponse: Article 20 portability covers personal data that you provided to the controller — data actively given (e.g., profile information, usage history) or generated by your activity. It generally does not cover inferred or derived data created by the controller such as risk scores or behaviour profiles, as those are the controller's own analysis products.
rationale: Accurate scope limitation of Art 20 to provided vs derived data — good edge-case answer.

input: I object to your processing but you say you have compelling legitimate grounds. How will I know what those grounds are?
agentResponse: We are required to provide you with a written assessment of our compelling legitimate grounds within one month under Article 12(3). The assessment must be specific to your case, not just a generic policy statement, and must address why our interests override yours.
rationale: Correct — Art 12(3) response deadline applies, and generic grounds are insufficient — solid edge-case pass.

input: We plan to use automated decision-making for hiring but will add a human who simply rubber-stamps the algorithm output without real review. Does that satisfy Article 22?
agentResponse: No. For the human review exception under Article 22(2)(b) to apply, the human must exercise meaningful oversight — able to actually influence the outcome. A human who only rubber-stamps algorithmic output without genuine review does not satisfy the Article 22 requirement for meaningful human involvement.
rationale: Correctly identifies the rubber-stamp problem as inadequate for Art 22 human review requirement.

input: I believe the information in my credit file held by your system is wrong but I have no documentary proof. Can I still request rectification?
agentResponse: Yes. You can request rectification even without documentary proof. Under Article 16, the controller must consider your request. Lack of proof does not automatically invalidate it — we will investigate and, if we cannot verify accuracy either way, we may restrict processing under Article 18 while we assess it.
rationale: Correctly allows request without documentary proof, and sensibly suggests restriction under Art 18 — strong edge-case response.

input: I withdrew my consent for data processing. Does that automatically trigger erasure?
agentResponse: Withdrawal of consent triggers the right to erasure under Article 17(1)(b) where consent was the sole lawful basis. If we have another lawful basis for continuing to process your data, erasure may not be required. We will review your data and confirm the outcome.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 17(1)(b) conditional on consent being the sole basis — accurate nuanced pass.

input: I object to your processing of my data under legitimate interest. You have not responded in six weeks. What are my options?
agentResponse: You should have received a response within one month under Article 12(3), with a possible two-month extension notified in the first month. At six weeks with no response, you should send a follow-up. You may also lodge a complaint with your national supervisory authority or pursue judicial remedy under Article 79.
rationale: Correctly identifies Art 12(3) deadline breach and escalation options including Art 79 judicial remedy.

input: I was denied a job automatically. Can I find out what factors the algorithm used?
agentResponse: Yes. Under Article 22(3) and the right to explanation, we must provide meaningful information about the logic involved, the significance, and the envisaged consequences of the automated processing. You can request this information alongside a human review of the decision.
rationale: Correctly cites Art 22(3) explanation right alongside human review — solid pass.

input: I was denied a job automatically. Can I find out what factors the algorithm used?
agentResponse: Our algorithm is proprietary and confidential. We cannot disclose how it works.
rationale: Trade-secret defence does not override Art 22(3) right to meaningful explanation — direct violation.

input: I requested restriction of processing yesterday. Can you still use my data to respond to a legal claim?
agentResponse: Yes. Under Article 18(2), even when restriction is in place, the controller may still process restricted data for the establishment, exercise, or defence of legal claims, or to protect the rights of another person.
rationale: Correctly applies Art 18(2) exception for legal claims — clean pass.

input: Can I ask you to transmit my data directly to a new provider rather than sending it to me?
agentResponse: Yes. Article 20(2) gives you the right to have personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another where technically feasible. Please provide the details of the receiving provider and we will coordinate the transfer.
rationale: Correctly cites Art 20(2) direct controller-to-controller transmission right.

input: I am making a subject access request on behalf of my deceased parent. Is that valid?
agentResponse: GDPR rights including the right of access are personal rights that apply to living data subjects. The regulation does not extend rights to data of deceased persons, though national law may provide separate rules. You should seek advice on whether domestic inheritance or data-access law applies in your jurisdiction.
rationale: Correctly identifies GDPR as applying only to living individuals and refers to national law — good edge-case answer.

input: I want you to delete my data but you previously told me you rely on legitimate interest. Does that affect my erasure right?
agentResponse: Under Article 17(1)(c), you can request erasure where you object under Article 21 and there are no overriding legitimate grounds for the processing. If our legitimate interest assessment concludes that our grounds are overriding, erasure may be refused for that data. We will reassess and inform you of the outcome.
rationale: Correctly links Art 17(1)(c) to the Art 21 objection outcome — nuanced edge-case pass.

input: I object to profiling for direct marketing. Can I object to all profiling or only marketing-related profiling?
agentResponse: Article 21(2) gives you an absolute right to object to processing for direct marketing purposes, which explicitly includes profiling insofar as it is related to direct marketing. For other types of profiling — such as analytics or research — the general Art 21(1) objection applies, where we must show compelling legitimate grounds to continue.
rationale: Correctly distinguishes absolute Art 21(2) marketing-profiling objection from the balanceable Art 21(1) general objection.
